messages:
amanda: FYI - saw a transient cross-org flash on the Rollouts page. Select canary for org-A, then quick-switch to org-B and the quota widget briefly shows B's numbers under A. Seems like a cache/key issue, not a permissions leak.
raj: Can you repro? steps?
amanda: Yes on staging. Steps: /rollouts -> open canary for org-A -> open quota panel -> quick-switch to org-B. About 30-50% of attempts show the wrong numbers for ~200-500ms then correct.
sophie: :thinking_face: We prefetch metrics for the next org and set an affinity header. Router-v2 cache keys by path+query+user, IIRC. If prefetched-org header isn't included in the key, we could return stale body.
mike: HAR/traces useful. My gut says inproc route cache returned a previous payload while UI glued to the wrong org context during fast swaps.
amanda: Attached HAR shows requests like:
```
GET /internal/rollout/metrics?org=A
Host: internal.api.redwood
X-Prefetch-Org: pref-42
Cookie: sess=xyz
```
Then next request X-Prefetch-Org changes but UI rendered the cached response. router-v2 logs show route_cache hit=true, key="/internal/rollout/metrics?org=A|user:123"
ellie: We explicitly strip any X-* headers at the edge for CDN normalization. Internal caches should still be tenant-aware. Which cache served it - edge or internal?
amanda: Confirmed router-v2 inproc returned it (origin=router-v2 in logs). Edge didn't serve these internal endpoints.
sophie: Short-term: disable caching for rollout metric endpoints. Medium-term: include a canonical tenant piece in the cache key (auth_org) or whitelist a signed internal header like X-RD-Prefetched-Org and include it in key derivation.
mike: Add telemetry: emit an event when auth_org != payload.org with fields route, cache_key, auth_org, payload_org. Alert on >3 mismatches/min.
raj: Agreed. Also add a UI banner on the rollout card when mismatch detected: "Stale data detected, refreshing..." to reduce user confusion.
amanda: I'll open a quick PR to invalidate route cache on org-switch events and add the banner. Also propose disabling caching on staging now.
ellie: Make it a canary rollout for prod. And add an e2e that rapidly switches orgs and asserts no cross-org rows in the quota widget. Also ensure edge still strips sensitive headers.
sophie: Created ticket RWF-487: "rollouts: prefetch isolation + rapid-switch e2e".
deploy-bot: Deployed router-v2:2026.3.2 to staging. Watch logs in #eng-oncall.
mike: I'll add the telemetry rule and pager if mismatch-rate spike.
amanda: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1157 - changes: route cache key now includes X-RD-Prefetched-Org (signed) + auth_org fallback; invalidation on quick-switch; UI banner; staging cache disabled.
raj: Please add unit tests for cache-key derivation and a flaky-tolerant e2e for rapid switch.
sophie: Also doc update: internal headers whitelist and signing policy so we don't accidentally trust arbitrary X-RD-* values.
ellie: After merge, let's run a 30m soak on staging then canary 5% prod for 1h before wider rollout.
amanda: Thanks team — will follow up with PR comments and a short postmortem if we see any regressions.
